subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient preserve unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in maxReconnectAttempts mode, impose a default retry ceiling, or leave reconnect policy unchanged and focus only on listener cleanup?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the default retry behavior is compatibility-sensitive because node-host recovery may intentionally rely on indefinite reconnects.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep existing default behavior for long-lived node clients and add a caller-controlled maxReconnectAttempts path for short-lived clients.

options.title: Default retry ceiling
options.body: Apply a default cap for every GatewayClient user, accepting upgrade risk for clients that currently rely on indefinite recovery.

options.title: Preserve policy and fix cleanup only
options.body: Leave reconnect attempts unlimited and pursue only concrete socket/listener cleanup if maintainers decide accumulation is the actual bug.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep existing default behavior for long-lived node clients and add a caller-controlled maxReconnectAttempts path for short-lived clients.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent package-client extraction and release-adjacent gateway work make this the best available routing candidate for the current implementation boundary.
